cards.text: Jesus wraps up His teaching to the people and heads to Capernaum. There, a centurion, an army officer, has a servant he values highly. And that servant is sick and about to die.

cards.question: The centurion hears about Jesus and wants Him to come heal his servant. So he sends some Jewish ___ to ask Him.

cards.text: The elders come to Jesus and plead with Him earnestly, "This man is worthy to have You grant this," and friend, these elders show up like a reference letter with LEGS.

cards.question: The elders tell Jesus the centurion is worthy. What reason do they give?

answers.text: He loves our nation and built our synagogue
He feeds our poor and keeps the Sabbath
He fasts often and gives to the temple

cards.text: So Jesus goes with them. He's not far from the house when the centurion sends friends with a message, like that text that hits right as you pull into the driveway.

cards.question: True or false: The centurion's message tells Jesus to hurry inside before it's too late.

cards.text: Instead the message begins, "Lord, do not trouble Yourself," and friend, the man is turning down a house call from JESUS.

cards.question: The centurion tells Jesus not to trouble Himself coming to the house. What reason does the centurion give?

answers.text: He isn't worthy to have Jesus under his roof
His house isn't ready for a guest
His servant is too sick for visitors

cards.question: The centurion doesn't feel worthy to have Jesus under his roof. True or false: He says that's also why he didn't come to Jesus himself.
The centurion doesn't want Jesus to trouble Himself coming under his roof. So what does the centurion ask Jesus to do so his servant will be healed?

cards.text: Then the centurion explains how he sees it: "For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me." This man knows a thing or two about giving orders.

cards.question: True or false: The centurion says his soldiers argue with him before they obey his orders.

cards.text: He says, "I tell one to go, and he goes, and another to come, and he comes." Friend, I set my oven timer for twelve minutes once, and it went off whenever it FELT like it.

cards.question: Jesus hears the centurion's message about orders and authority. How does Jesus react to the centurion?

cards.text: Jesus turns to the crowd following Him, and He's got something to say about this centurion's faith. Friend, the only thing I ever made marvel was a smoke alarm, and that wasn't marveling, that was SCREAMING.

cards.question: Jesus tells the crowd following Him that not even in ___ has He found such great faith.
True or false: When the messengers return to the centurion's house, they find the servant in good health.

findings.problem: From card 4 to card 14 the choice cards strictly alternate multiple choice and true or false: 4 MC, 6 TF, 8 MC, 9 TF, 10 MC, 12 TF, 14 MC. The question types follow a fixed pattern instead of being chosen for each card.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: The centurion's authority comparison (Luke 7:8) is the heart of his faith. Card 11 sets it up with 'explains how he sees it', but no card asks what the comparison means: that Jesus can command the healing with a word, the way the centurion's orders are carried out. Card 12 only asks a surface detail about soldiers arguing. The line 'I tell my servant to do something, and he does it' is also never told, even though it ties the picture back to the sick servant.

rule.text: These rules apply to every passage, of any type: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: The question asks how Jesus reacts to the centurion. 'He marvels at him' and 'He rebukes him' are reactions, but 'He goes inside anyway' is a movement. It isn't the same kind of thing as the other two answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Galilee and Jerusalem are both inside Israel, and Jesus is in Galilee (Capernaum) at this moment. A baker could argue that 'not even in Galilee' or 'not even in Jerusalem' means close to the same thing as 'not even in Israel'.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
